item.text: The two specification mismatches are clear: year-end selection only rounds backward instead of choosing the nearest Saturday, and a 53rd week is currently added to period 1 instead of period 12. I’m checking the full test behavior now, then I’ll make the smallest targeted fix and add boundary coverage if needed.

item.text: The implementation is patched: year ends now choose the Saturday on either side of January 31 by actual distance, and the 53rd week extends period 12. I’m running the complete suite and a few calendar-invariant checks next.

item.command:
/usr/bin/zsh -lc "python3 -m unittest discover -v && python3 - <<'PY'
from datetime import date, timedelta
from fiscal.calendar import fiscal_year_end, fiscal_year_start, weeks_in_year, fiscal_week, period_bounds

for fy in range(2000, 2041):
    start, end = fiscal_year_start(fy), fiscal_year_end(fy)
    assert (end - start).days + 1 in (364, 371)
    assert weeks_in_year(fy) == ((end - start).days + 1) // 7
    assert fiscal_week(start)[1] == 1
    assert fiscal_week(end)[1] == weeks_in_year(fy)
    assert period_bounds(fy, 1)[0] == start
    assert period_bounds(fy, 12)[1] == end
print('calendar invariants: ok')
PY
git diff -- fiscal/calendar.py && git status --short"

item.text:
Fixed `fiscal/calendar.py`:

- Year ends now use the Saturday nearest January 31, including early-February dates.
- 53-week years assign the extra week to period 12.
- Early-February sales now map to the correct fiscal year.

Validation passed: all 18 tests plus calendar invariant checks.
